figures.title: Generating text one token at a time
figures.desc: The prompt 'HashSet iteration order is' is tokenized. The model scores every possible next token; 'not' is most likely and is appended. The model then scores again with the longer text, picks 'guaranteed' and appends it. The loop repeats until a stop token or the maximum output length.
figures.heading: Next-token prediction loop

steps.caption: The prompt is split into tokens and sent to the model
The model gives a probability to every possible next token
One token is chosen – usually a likely one
"not" is appended; the longer text goes back into the model
Repeat token by token until a stop token or the output limit

figures.title: Temperature and top-p on one distribution

figures.title: Token bucket with capacity 5 and refill 2 per second
figures.desc: The bucket starts full with 5 tokens. Five requests at the same instant each spend one token and are allowed, leaving the bucket empty. A sixth request at that instant finds no token and is rejected with 429. Tokens refill at 2 per second, so half a second later one token is back and the next request is allowed.
figures.heading: Token bucket: capacity 5, refill 2 tokens/second

The next request spends it and is allowed

figures.title: Cache-aside reads and writes
figures.desc: Read: the app asks the cache for the key. On a hit it returns the cached value. On a miss it reads the database, puts the value in the cache with a TTL and returns it. Write: the app updates the database first and then deletes the cache key, so the next read loads the fresh value.
figures.heading: Cache-aside: the application owns loading and invalidation

figures.title: LRU eviction with room for three entries
figures.desc: The cache holds at most three entries, ordered from most to least recently used. Put A, then B, then C gives C, B, A. Reading A moves it to the front: A, C, B. Putting D when full evicts the least recently used entry, B, giving D, A, C.
figures.heading: LRU: evict the least recently used entry

nodes.label:
put B, put C
[C, B, A]

steps.caption: Capacity 3. Put A: the list holds [A] (front = most recent)
Put B and C: newest first, [C, B, A]
Reading A moves it to the front: [A, C, B]
Put D while full: remove from the back – B is least recently used
Result [D, A, C]: hash map for O(1) lookup, linked list for O(1) reordering

figures.title: Adding a node to a consistent hash ring
figures.desc: Nodes A, B, C and D sit around a hash ring, and each key belongs to the next node clockwise. Keys k1 and k2 hash between B and C, so before the change they belong to C; key k3 hashes between C and D and belongs to D. When node E is added between k2 and C, only k1 and k2 move to E. k3 and every other key stay where they were.
figures.heading: Consistent hashing: adding E moves only one arc of keys

steps.caption: Nodes A-D sit on a ring of hash values; a key belongs to the next node clockwise
k1 and k2 hash between B and C, so (before E exists) C owns them; k3 belongs to D
Add node E on the ring between k2 and C
Now the next node clockwise from k1 and k2 is E: only they move
k3 still goes to D and every other arc is untouched; hash % N would move most keys

figures.title: Notification pipeline
figures.desc: A business event is accepted once by the notification service, which de-duplicates by event ID and saves it. Preferences decide which channels to use. One message per channel goes to its own queue. Channel workers render the template and call the provider. A temporary failure goes back to the queue with exponential backoff; after the last attempt the message goes to a dead-letter queue. Success records SENT.

figures.desc: The user selects seats. holdSeats checks every seat under the show lock; if any seat is taken the request fails and nothing changes. If payment succeeds and the booking still holds its seats, the seats are booked and the booking is confirmed. If payment fails or the hold expired, the seats are released and any late payment is refunded.

figures.title: ATM state machine
figures.desc: Idle: inserting a card moves to HasCard. HasCard: a correct PIN moves to Authenticated; a wrong PIN stays in HasCard until the third failure, which ejects the card and returns to Idle; cancel also ejects to Idle. Authenticated: balance inquiry and withdrawal keep the machine in Authenticated; ejecting the card returns to Idle.
figures.heading: ATM states (State pattern)

steps.caption: The ATM waits in IdleState; only insertCard does anything
A card is inserted: the ATM moves to HasCardState
A wrong PIN keeps it in HasCardState (2 tries left)
The bank confirms the correct PIN: AuthenticatedState
Balance and withdraw are only possible here
Eject card: back to IdleState for the next customer

figures.title: ATM classes
figures.desc: ATM is the context. It holds one current ATMState, the inserted Card, a Screen, a CashDispenser and a BankService. IdleState, HasCardState and AuthenticatedState implement the ATMState interface with insertCard, enterPin, checkBalance, withdraw and ejectCard. BankService authenticates, returns balances, debits and reverses. CashDispenser plans and dispenses notes. The ATM records Transactions.

figures.title: Cab booking classes
figures.desc: RideService manages Trips and uses a MatchingStrategy to find candidate drivers, a FareStrategy to estimate and calculate fares, and a NotificationService to send offers and updates. A Trip links one Rider and, after acceptance, one Driver, with pickup and drop Locations, a TripStatus and a fare. A Driver has a Vehicle with a VehicleType, a current Location and a DriverStatus that is claimed atomically.

figures.title: Trip lifecycle
figures.desc: A trip starts REQUESTED. When a driver accepts it becomes DRIVER_ASSIGNED, then DRIVER_ARRIVED when the driver reaches the pickup, IN_PROGRESS when the rider is picked up, and COMPLETED at the drop, when the fare is calculated and the driver is released. The rider can cancel from REQUESTED, DRIVER_ASSIGNED or DRIVER_ARRIVED, which moves the trip to CANCELLED and releases any assigned driver.

Bilal's accept runs the same compareAndSet, finds D1 already ON_TRIP and fails, so Bilal's trip T2 stays REQUESTED and the offer moves to the next driver, D2.
